themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Missing complaints spiked to 4 this week versus 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (357% increase, z-score 4.0), suggesting coordinated removal, theft, or maintenance failure affecting wayfinding and traffic safety in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 4 street sign complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike)
Z-score of 4.0 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Pattern suggests concentrated geographic or temporal trigger this week
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: map the missing signs, interview DOT about maintenance schedules
Investigation: are signs being stolen for scrap or damaged by construction?

themes_detail.label: Tree Overgrowth Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown Tree/Branches complaints jumped to 28 this week from 7.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score 5.12), the sharpest sustained environmental complaint surge, suggesting deferred maintenance or weather-triggered rapid growth blocking sidewalks and sightlines.
evidence: 28 overgrown tree complaints this week vs. 7.5 weekly average (273% increase)
Z-score of 5.12 indicates highly significant spike
Coincides with recent warm/wet weather window; may reflect Parks Dept capacity issues
Community board has repeatedly requested better park maintenance funding
reporting_angles: Witness reporting: photograph affected streets, identify neighborhood clusters of complaints
Policy angle: does Parks Dept have sufficient crew capacity to respond to spring growth surge?
Follow-up: tie to recurring community board budget request for park maintenance

themes_detail.label: Noise From Vehicles Spiking
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Vehicle complaints surged to 10 this week versus 2.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (264% increase, z-score 4.64), indicating potential illegal modifications, street racing, or delivery truck congestion emerging this week.
evidence: 10 vehicle noise complaints this week vs. 2.8 weekly average (264% spike)
Z-score of 4.64 indicates highly significant anomaly
Complements existing high baseline of 1,965 illegal parking complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Door-knock residents on loudest complaint blocks to identify time-of-day patterns and vehicle types
Investigate: are modified exhausts, street racing, or overnight delivery trucks the culprit?
NYPD coordination: check if precinct has noted related complaints or enforcement activity

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Posting complaints skyrocketed to 4 last week from 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 7.49—highest z-score in dataset), suggesting rapid campaign of graffiti, unauthorized flyers, or signage that requires urgent investigation of source and scope.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% increase)
Highest z-score in entire dataset (7.49), indicating extreme statistical anomaly
May indicate coordinated posting campaign or recent enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Street canvass: document what type of illegal postings (ads, political, graffiti) and where concentrated
Source investigation: are these related to a single campaign or multiple bad actors?

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb Condition complaints spiked to 9 this week from 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score 5.3), reflecting potential potholes, crumbling concrete, or recent vehicle impacts that align with the district's recurring requests for street reconstruction.
evidence: 9 curb condition complaints this week vs. 1.5 weekly average (500% increase)
Z-score of 5.3 indicates highly significant spike
Correlates with 2,368 street condition complaints over 90 days (district's top complaint type)
Community board has requested street reconstruction funding year after year (unmet need)
reporting_angles: Photo essay: map the worst curb damage this week, measure severity
DOT accountability: when will repairs happen, and is this connected to winter damage or heavy vehicle traffic?
Policy: tie recurring complaint to chronic underfunding of street maintenance
